prompt: My landlord is refusing essential roof repairs and rain is damaging my personal furniture.
expected: Outlines landlord's statutory duty to maintain premises; habitability rights; duty of mitigation.

raw_response.content:
I can help you with this. Here's a clear overview based on Indian law and typical tenancy principles.

### | Your Situation
You have vacated the property and your landlord is not returning the the disputed amount security deposit (held for an extended period) in your city. This is a tenancy-related dispute about return of the deposit.

### | Your Legal Position
* A security deposit is meant to cover unpaid rent or actual damages, not routine wear and tear.
* **The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Section 11)** – provides that a security deposit should be returned after adjusting lawful dues. Its applicability may depend on state adoption.
* **General principles under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Section 108)** – the tenant must return the property in a reasonable condition, subject to normal wear and tear.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. **Gather evidence** – rental agreement (if any), payment records (UPI/bank), handover photos, and WhatsApp/emails with the landlord.
2. **Send a written demand** – request return of the the disputed amount with a reasonable time (e.g., 7–15 days).
3. **If unresolved** – you may consider a complaint before the local Rent Authority or a civil suit for recovery of money.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What is the exact amount of money (in ₹) involved in this dispute?

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Relief against forfeiture and prohibition against cutting off essential supplies
citations.description: No landlord shall without just or sufficient cause cut off or withhold any essential supply or service (water, electricity, lifts) enjoyed by the tenant. Violation is punishable with imprisonment or fine.

citations.title: Protection of tenant against eviction and restoration of essential amenities
citations.description: Strict grounds required for eviction; prohibits withholding essential amenities without reasonable cause. Tenant may approach Rent Controller for summary restoration.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.
